desc:
A single machine works through jobs one at a time. Every job takes exactly one unit of time, and the machine starts at time 0, so the jobs it runs occupy the time slots 1, 2, 3, … Job i earns profits[i] but only if it finishes by its deadline: it must be placed in a slot that is at most deadlines[i]. A job can be skipped, and each job can run at most once.

Return the largest total profit that can be earned.

deadlines = [2, 1, 2, 1, 3], profits = [100, 19, 27, 25, 15] -> 142
deadlines = [4, 1, 1, 1], profits = [20, 10, 40, 30]          -> 60
deadlines = [1, 1, 1], profits = [5, 6, 7]                    -> 7

In the first example run the job worth 27 in slot 1, the job worth 100 in slot 2 and the job worth 15 in slot 3.
hints: Whatever set of jobs you pick, a feasible schedule exists if and only if the jobs can be placed in distinct slots up to their deadlines. Which jobs are the most worth fighting for a slot?
Consider jobs from the highest profit to the lowest. Take a job if it can still get a slot; put it in the latest free slot not after its deadline, so earlier slots stay free for tighter jobs.

Finding the latest free slot quickly: deadlines can be capped at n (you never run more than n jobs). Use a union-find over slots where each used slot points to the slot before it, or sort by deadline and use a min-heap of chosen profits.
editorial: Sort the jobs by profit, largest first. Process them in that order and try to give each one the latest free slot that is not after its deadline. If there is one, the job is scheduled; otherwise it is dropped. Choosing the latest slot is safe because it leaves all earlier slots free for jobs with shorter deadlines. Accepting a job whenever it fits is safe because the sets of schedulable jobs form a matroid, so the greedy by weight gives an optimal set.

Because at most n jobs can run, cap every deadline at n. To find the latest free slot at or before d quickly, keep a union-find array parent[s] where a used slot links to s - 1; slot 0 means no free slot. After placing a job, link its slot to the slot before it.

An alternative with the same result: sort the jobs by deadline, push each profit into a min-heap, and whenever the heap holds more jobs than the current deadline allows, pop the smallest profit. Both run in O(n log n).
